now.title: 3.11 is out. Next is 3.12, Read aloud
now.note: 3.11, Files you bring in, is released. It sorts the files you bring in, from your own test of Find my files. 3.9 (Records with the suite) and 3.10 (versions of a record, web clips from Recon Browser, and a look like the rest of the family) came before it.

items.title: 3.11: files you bring in
items.text: Find my files sorts by type, with a files view and sections for audio, art and covers, and the app can check that folder for changes. Also a Look choice of Solid, Metallic or Glass, lists you can resize and fold, right-click menus, a bigger apps window, fixes for small windows and small screens and for a manuscript dropped in favour of its copy, and other apps are now told this one takes web clips as research.

items.title: Records
items.text: Characters, places, weapons or your own kinds, with links both ways, @ in a chapter, saved views, numbering and bringing records in from files.

items.title: The suite
items.text: The apps finding each other when installed, an Apps panel, a status line and a book’s word count on request. Webhooks and n8n are left for their own design.

items.title: 3.10: versions of a record
items.text: Freeze a record for each book, with a printable part and an author-only part, canon lock, and records printed as a PDF with a label like Record 0100 · Revision 2. A frozen version can never be changed or unfrozen.

items.title: Web clips from Recon Browser
items.text: Recon Browser sends research to this app over App Link. A clip waits in the inbox, and nothing is filed or fetched without your choice. A locked project holds it until you unlock it.

items.title: Apps status icon
items.text: A small icon on the toolbar with a dot that shows whether other Recon Towers apps are linked, found or off, and opens a panel that lists every app with what you can do about it. It says it in words as well as colour.

items.title: Updates in the Apps panel
items.text: The panel says when another Recon Towers app has a newer version, with both numbers and a button to update or download it. It never stops two apps linking: only an incompatible link protocol does, and then it says which app needs an update. Nothing about you is sent when it checks.

items.title: Looks like the rest of the family
items.text: A Help menu like RT Markdown Reader's with a Help Center and Keyboard Shortcuts, an About window with links and copyable version details, and a bar across the top of the library with Preferences, so the themes can be found before a project is open. Any of the app's shortcuts can be changed, from the Help menu or Preferences. Preferences is now a window with its sections down the side. A tutorial and a find-a-command box are still to come.

items.title: Still open from earlier
items.text: Your own test of the lock and of Find my files, a real Word manuscript, Pages on a Mac, and a real Scrivener project.

items.title: Released before this
items.text: 3.11.0 is the latest release. Before it came 3.10.0, 3.9.0, and 3.7.2, which let Find my files see OneDrive files on Windows.

items.title: Next, from your own testing
items.text: Read aloud, built into this app, with highlighting and letter colours like Word’s that shift their shade so they stay easy to read, and a safer way to pick up an unfinished import (3.12). After read aloud, still in 3.12, this app’s Solid, Metallic and Glass looks are to come from the suite’s shared theme repository, with the Look choice and the colour behaviour kept. Then Connect Claude (3.13), with your choice of how much it may do and a record of every change it makes. Writing patterns, a check across a book or series for repeated words, stock phrases AI overuses and your own banned phrases, is on the roadmap as 3.24 and waits for your go. When you give it, it moves up to just after 3.13. Features more than one app needs, such as read aloud and your own AI service, are to come from one shared code module. It isn’t created yet and waits for your go. Publishing to blogs and wikis from inside this app is on the roadmap as 3.25, as you decided. It comes from the shared code module, so it depends on that module, which isn’t created yet and waits for your go. Your sign-ins are to be kept inside the Lock, and RT Markdown Reader can still publish over App Link. Nothing is being built yet.

waiting.title: A test and {decisions} decisions
waiting.text: Your own tests of Records and printing on Windows and Mac, a real power cut during a lock, and the decisions below.

questions.q: Can the apps detect each other when they’re installed?
questions.a: In 3.9, yes, for this app: it says it’s installed, and an Apps panel lists installed, running and linked apps. RT Markdown Reader needs the same change on its side before the two see each other when closed.
In Preferences, under Appearance. Preferences is the button at the top of the library, and it’s at the end of the Edit menu (Ctrl+,). On a Mac it’s in the app’s own menu.

questions.q: What happens to pictures in an imported file?
questions.a: From v3.5 they stay with the book as attachments, encrypted like the rest of the project. They sit beside the writing and don’t appear on the page yet.

questions.q: Why did StoryTracker move off WPF?
questions.a: WPF only runs on Windows. The new app is Electron and JavaScript, like RT Markdown Reader, so one app runs on Windows, Mac and Linux. The old C# code is kept in legacy-wpf.

questions.q: Does it use the same themes as RT Markdown Reader?
questions.a: The same set, as copies. It has all of RT Markdown Reader's themes, the old app's Plum, Evergreen, Blue/Orange and Aero, and a new one, Slate, with a Look of Solid, Metallic or Glass. A theme added to one app doesn't reach the other by itself yet. In 3.12, after read aloud, the three looks are to come from one shared theme repository. The rest of sharing themes, such as a theme you add once showing up in every app, is planned for later and waits for your go-ahead. From 3.11 it has the same Look choice as RT Markdown Reader. Colour-safe and Customize Theme come later, in v3.23.

Yes, in v3.12, with offline voices. It’s built into this app, so no other app is needed. Names said right, from the dictionary, and dictation follow in v3.22. All of it is to come from a shared code module, which isn’t created yet and waits for your go. If you also use RT Markdown Reader, you can send a chapter there and have it read, as a bonus.

questions.q: Will the dictionary know how to say words?
questions.a: Yes. In v3.15 each word can carry a pronunciation guide, for invented words and words from other languages. Read aloud in this app uses it, so a name is taught once. If RT Markdown Reader is linked, its voices can use it too over App Link, which is a bonus you don’t need.

questions.q: Can more themes and fonts be downloaded?
questions.a: Theme and font packs are under Later.

questions.q: Were these features taken from RT Markdown Reader?
questions.a: Partly. Most came from what you said you need. In November the two roadmaps were compared feature by feature, and what this app was missing was added: v3.8, v3.21 to v3.23, and wider v3.15 and v3.17. Since 27 November 2026, a feature more than one app needs is to come from one shared code module, not a copy in each. The module isn’t created yet and waits for your go. Nobody has to install the Reader to use this app.

questions.q: How do I hand an AI a chapter as Markdown?
questions.a: Export the chapter as Markdown. That’s built into this app, from v3.3. Claude can work with the book directly in v3.13. If you also use RT Markdown Reader, App Link can send a chapter there too, as a bonus (v3.7 or later).

questions.q: Can it be tested on real stories?
questions.a: Yes, once the basics work. Your stories and Notion become the test bed, and what you need for how you write goes on this roadmap.

questions.q: Will it make EPUBs that KDP accepts?
questions.a: It makes EPUBs that pass EPUBCheck, the official validator, with no errors or warnings. The test that counts is uploading one to KDP’s previewer, which is yours to do. The EPUB, Word and PDF exports are built into this app, so it makes them on its own. They’re to come from the shared code module once it exists.
